definitions.explanation: a heated verbal exchange or disagreement between people

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{口論|こうろん}になった。
examples.english: The two got into an argument.

examples.japanese: {些細|ささい}なことで{口論|こうろん}した。
{口論|こうろん}の{末|すえ}、{彼|かれ}は{部屋|へや}を{出|で}て{行|い}った。
examples.english: After the argument, he left the room.

notes:
FORMATION:
{口|こう} (mouth) + {論|ろん} (argument, discussion) → verbal argument

VERB FORM:
{口論|こうろん}する (to argue, to quarrel)

RELATED WORDS:
- {喧嘩|けんか} (fight, quarrel - can include physical)
- {言|い}い{争|あらそ}い (verbal dispute)
- {論争|ろんそう} (debate, controversy - more formal)
- {揉|も}め{事|ごと} (trouble, dispute)
- {口喧嘩|くちげんか} (verbal fight)

DISTINCTION:
{口論|こうろん} is specifically verbal and somewhat formal. {喧嘩|けんか} is more casual and can include physical fighting. {口喧嘩|くちげんか} is a casual word specifically for verbal fighting.
